newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutz aims boost return to industry norm.
newsitem.headline: Deutz aims boost return to industry norm.

text.p: Deutz AG, the German machinery maker reborn from the rubble of Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, said on Friday it aimed to boost returns to the level of its competitors.
Chief executive Anton Schneider said in an interview with the Handelsblatt daily that pretax margins of five to 10 percent of sales were the norm in the sector.
"For us too it must be five percent," he said, without saying what Deutz's return is now. The company also aims to reduce its debt sharply.

Schneider said restructuring is proceeding smoothly. The company expects to post a group net profit of 870 million to 880 million marks for 1996, swinging from a 1.13 billion mark loss the previous year, the result of hidden losses on contracts to build cement plants in Saudi Arabia.

"We are over the hump, but we are still not good," Schneider said. The company expects to post a profit this year as well, with which it will replenish losses, but great efforts will still be needed to make it fit, he said.
Reductions in personnel and production costs, and simplification of the corporate structure were the main reasons for the improvement in results, he said.

Production facilities in Cologne, for example, were now concentrated on one-fifth of the previous area. Production volumes must now be increased, particularly for motors, he said. The company must build up its presence in regional markets such as eastern Europe. It is already well represented in the U.S., he said.
The company was rescued last year in a spectacular billion-mark bailout by its creditor banks, led by Deutsche Bank AG.
